name: Gmail (Google)
use_case: read, search and send email in users' Gmail inboxes

verdict.label: Gated · approval not guaranteed
verdict.summary: Building is easy, but reading users' mail requires Google's restricted-scope verification and a paid, annual third-party security assessment (CASA). Plan for weeks, and pick your scopes before you write code, because the scope decides the path.
verdict.active_effort: 1–2 days of prep (policies, video, domain checks) plus fixing security-scan findings
verdict.wait: Brand verification 2–3 business days; restricted-scope review plus CASA is typically several weeks (Google publishes no fixed time)
verdict.gating_step: Restricted-scope verification plus the CASA Tier 2 security assessment

concept: In Google Cloud, your OAuth app is a Cloud project with a configured consent screen (the Google Auth Platform: Branding, Audience, Data Access) and an OAuth client ID. What Google reviews is the project's requested scopes, not your code. Every user who connects authorizes that project. The 100-user cap for unverified apps applies over the project's entire lifetime.

paths.name: Sign-in only
paths.when: You only need openid, email and profile.

paths.name: Send only (gmail.send)
paths.when: The agent drafts and sends but never reads the inbox. gmail.send is a sensitive scope, not restricted, so there's no security assessment.
paths.wait: 2–3 business days brand plus 3–5 business days sensitive-scope review

paths.name: Read or modify the mailbox (gmail.readonly / gmail.modify)
paths.when: The agent reads, searches or labels mail. Restricted scope: verification plus an annual CASA assessment.

composio.managed_note: Composio's Gmail toolkit has a Composio-managed OAuth app, so you can build and pilot without going through Google's review yourself. Users will see Composio on the consent screen.
when_own_app: Production: users should see your app name on the consent screen, not “Composio”.
You need scopes beyond Composio's defaults.
You need your own rate-limit quota (managed apps share quota across Composio users).
You need faster polling triggers than the managed 15-minute minimum.
Self-hosted or regional instances of the provider.

stages.name: Build & test (works today, with limits)
stages.summary: You can build and test immediately in Testing mode, but only with hand-picked test users and weekly re-consent.

limits.text: Testing mode is limited to 100 test users listed on the consent screen.
In Testing, test users' authorizations expire 7 days after consent, refresh tokens included. Connections silently break every week.
Unverified apps are capped at 100 users over the project's lifetime, and the cap can't be reset. The Audience page shows it as a meter (“0 users (0 test, 0 other) / 100 user cap”).

steps.title: Create a dedicated Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Use one project for production and a separate one for development and testing. Each gets its own 100 test users, and production stays clean for review.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: APIs & Services → Library → Gmail API → Enable.

steps.title: Branding: app name, support email, developer contact
steps.detail: In Google Auth Platform → Get started → app name, user support email, audience (External) and contact email. Keep these accurate; Google uses the contact emails for review requests, and missed emails can stall or revoke access.

steps.title: Audience: External + Testing, add test users
steps.detail: New apps start in “Testing”. With a personal account (project in “No organization”), “Make internal” is greyed out, so External is your only choice. Add your own and pilot users' Google accounts under Test users.

steps.title: Data Access: add only the scopes you need
steps.detail: Use “Add or remove scopes”. If a scope isn't listed (only enabled APIs' scopes are), paste the full URL under “Manually add scopes” → Add to table → Update. The page then sorts scopes into non-sensitive, sensitive and restricted sections. In our test, gmail.send landed under sensitive and gmail.readonly under restricted (“Gmail scopes”). This choice decides your whole review path.

steps.title: Clients: create an OAuth client (Web application)
steps.detail: Add Composio's callback URL under “Authorized redirect URIs”, then copy the client ID and secret into a Composio auth config.

steps.title: Connect a test user end to end
steps.detail: Expect the “Google hasn't verified this app” warning. That's normal in Testing.

stages.name: Go to production
stages.summary: Brand verification first, then scope verification, then (for restricted scopes) the CASA security assessment. You only get the assessment step after Google's Trust & Safety team reaches out.

steps.title: Verify every domain on the consent screen
steps.detail: Homepage, privacy policy and authorized domains must be verified in Google Search Console by a project owner or editor.

steps.title: Publish a privacy policy that meets Limited Use
steps.detail: Restricted scopes require your policy to disclose Limited Use of Google user data. Google publishes examples of policies that fail.

steps.title: Write a justification per scope
steps.detail: Explain why each sensitive or restricted scope is needed and why a narrower one isn't enough.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Show the full consent flow with your OAuth client ID visible in the browser address bar, then show each feature that uses each scope.

steps.title: Complete Branding, publish, and submit for verification
steps.detail: “Publish app” stays greyed out until the Branding page is complete (homepage, privacy policy and so on). Brand verification typically takes 2–3 business days; sensitive scopes typically 3–5 business days. Restricted scopes have no published time.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: Google contacts you when it's time. Pick an authorized lab (Google points developers to TAC Security, whose Tier 2 basic plan was listed at $540 per app), fix the scan findings, and receive a Letter of Validation. Repeat every 12 months.

requirements.detail: Every domain on the consent screen, verified in Search Console.
Required for sensitive and restricted scopes.
Showing the consent flow, client ID and each scope in use.
Restricted scopes only. Renewed every 12 months from the previous Letter of Validation.
Third-party lab fee. TAC Security listed Tier 2 at $540 per app (basic plan) at the time of research.

gotchas.title: Scope choice decides your timeline
gotchas.detail: gmail.send is sensitive (days). gmail.readonly and gmail.modify are restricted (weeks plus CASA). Using the broad mail.google.com scope just to send via SMTP violates Google's minimum-scope policy.

gotchas.title: Testing-mode tokens die after 7 days
gotchas.detail: Pilot users' connections silently expire weekly until you're verified. Warn pilots, or pilot on Composio's managed app instead.

gotchas.title: The 100-user cap is for life
gotchas.detail: Unverified projects can't reset it. Don't burn it on internal testing; use a separate dev project.

gotchas.title: Workspace admins can still block you
gotchas.detail: Even when verified, a customer's Google Workspace admin may restrict third-party apps or high-risk Gmail scopes.

gotchas.title: Consent screen and Data Access scopes must match
gotchas.detail: Reviewers reject submissions where the scopes you request at runtime differ from those declared in Cloud Console.

blockers.cause: Your request includes sensitive or restricted scopes that aren't approved yet.
blockers.fix: In Testing, add the user as a test user. For real users, complete verification for those scopes.

blockers.cause: The user isn't on the test-user list while the app is in Testing, or a restricted scope isn't approved yet.
blockers.fix: Add them as a test user, or finish verification.

blockers.cause: The redirect URI isn't listed exactly under the OAuth client's Authorized redirect URIs.
blockers.fix: Add Composio's callback URL exactly, with no trailing slash differences.

blockers.cause: User type is Internal, and the user is outside your Google Cloud organization.

agent: Map each agent feature to the narrowest Gmail scope
Draft the Limited Use privacy-policy section
Write the demo-video shot list and script
Pre-check consent-screen fields against Google's branding requirements
you: Create the Cloud project and click through the consent-screen setup
Submit for verification and answer Google's emails promptly
Contract and pay the CASA lab, fix findings, renew yearly

uncertainties: Google publishes no fixed timeline for restricted-scope review. The 42-day figure used for scoring is our estimate, not Google's.
Which CASA tier Google assigns (Tier 2 vs Tier 3) is decided case by case.
Lab pricing comes from the lab's own site and may have changed.
